regressions.title: Post-polish claim-coverage check ignores placed_text, so narrative polish is always rejected (with a spurious report entry) whenever a transcript is placed under steps and the narrative paraphrases it
regressions.evidence: Static trace (no test covers paraphrasing narrative + placed transcript + polish enabled). narrative.py:46 now calls ensure_claim_coverage(text, claims, placed_text=placed_text), so a claim that is placed verbatim under a step is 'covered' and gets NO [verify] blockquote (claim_coverage.py:64). After polish, server.py:781 calls validate_claim_coverage(md_narrative_text or '', claims) WITHOUT placed_text; claim_coverage.py:84-88 then finds neither the claim text nor a [verify] marker in the narrative -> every placed-but-paraphrased claim is 'missing' -> report['polish_rejected_claim_coverage'] lists them and md_narrative_text reverts to the unpolished narrative (server.py:782-784). Before this branch those claims carried [verify] blockquotes inside narrative_text (spliced back verbatim by polish._splice_verify_lines), so the check passed. Effect: the narrative polish stage is silently dead for the common 'labelled transcript + paraphrasing narrative model' case and the sidecar reports a coverage failure that did not happen. The plan's own F-16 approach text specified `placed_text=` on this call. Fix: pass the same placed_text (join of step narrations) to validate_claim_coverage, which needs a `placed_text=''` keyword mirroring ensure_claim_coverage.
